Author: kirolosedward1
Message:
Log failed email sends so the retry job can recover them (#73)

* Log failed email sends so the retry job can recover them.

A claim that fails before any outbox row exists used to drop the message. Record status failed (retryable, gave_up_at unset) and, when the database client itself cannot write, report the template and recipient domain without throwing. The sweeper does not resend a row older than 48 hours.

Co-authored-by: kirolosedward1 <kirolosedward1@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep a lost claim from writing a second failed email row.

Look up the existing outbox row before the failure fallback insert. A keyed attempt uses dedupe_key with an upsert that ignores duplicates. An attempt with no key is matched on entity id, template, recipient, and a two-minute created_at window, because a null dedupe_key is not unique. Bound that write to 3 seconds. Treat an unreadable email age as outside the 48-hour window.

Co-authored-by: kirolosedward1 <kirolosedward1@users.noreply.github.com>

* Drop the time-window match for failed email rows.

Duplicate protection for a lost claim is the dedupe_key upsert only. A send with no key always inserts its own failed row, because two applicants to the same job share entity, template, and recipient.

Co-authored-by: kirolosedward1 <kirolosedward1@users.noreply.github.com>

* Give each email attempt an id before the claim insert.

The failure fallback upserts that same id, so a claim that committed and then timed out stays one row even without a dedupe key. Two attempts still get two rows. dedupeKey is required on DeliverySpec, and a dedupe key still refuses a second attempt.

Co-authored-by: kirolosedward1 <kirolosedward1@users.noreply.github.com>

Author: Claude
Message:
Round 11: hidden lists with a way back; email links that never switch accounts unasked

Hidden companies and consultants
- Account → "Hidden on this phone" lists them by name, each with "Show
  again". Hiding takes them out of every list, so their own pages, where the
  way back was, were out of reach; the confirmation now points here. The store
  keeps the name each was hidden under, and still reads a list of bare ids.
- Totals leave hidden rows out (the board, the companies, the directory,
  the shortlist's count), and the Arabic confirm for a consultant is his own
  word, not the company's feminine one.

Sign-in
- An email link is checked with a client that keeps nothing before its
  session is taken: Supabase answers with the session of whoever the token
  belongs to, so a new-address link someone sent for an account of theirs
  signed the person holding the phone into it, unasked. Now the account is
  known first: nobody signed in, or the same one, it is taken; another, the
  person is asked, naming both.
- A link opened again (or late) by the person already signed in says it is
  spent, with nothing to sign in to; signed out, "sign in" keeps where the link
  was going.
- Sign-up waits while its config cannot be read, says so, and reads it again
  on asking, rather than going without the check Supabase asks for, every
  time; `captcha_failed` has its own sentence, here and on the website.
- Google stands alone in Expo Go, where Apple's sign-in cannot work.
- The website asks every account with an authenticator for its code before
  any page of the account, as its own page promises, and the account page
  draws nothing but the challenge until it is answered, then goes on to where
  the person was going. The database still asks it of admins only: written
  down in the threat model as its own release.

Author: Claude
Message:
App round 10, part 2: VoiceOver, lists, cold start, sessions, pushes

- VoiceOver: a job card says everything it shows (sponsored, closed,
  applied to, the pay and the rest), and onboarding's agreement offers the
  Terms and the Privacy policy as actions, which it could not reach inside
  the checkbox.
- A refused or unanswered withdrawal reads the applications again, so the
  row shows where the application stands instead of its Withdraw button.
- Reaching the end of a list while it is being read again no longer cancels
  that read (TanStack's fetchNextPage did, leaving a cold start's kept
  board as it was); the next page follows once the read is in.
- Cold start: an opening list whose last re-read failed is kept as the
  answer it had; nothing is drawn until the phone has said which companies
  the reader hid; the board keeps its filters and an open filter sheet when
  its first read fails; "Clear filters" keeps the pinned company while the
  board loads.
- A call to the website while the session cannot be refreshed is said as
  no answer, rather than sent without the person's token and answered as a
  stranger's.
- Another account taking over the phone through an email link stops the
  last person's pushes before the new registration; a password-reset link
  for another account clears the last person's data from the screen.
- Expo Go workflow: the commit message's first line is taken in the shell,
  by characters (cut counted bytes).

Each has a test that fails without it. A session test file no longer keeps
Jest waiting five minutes for TanStack's cache timer.

Message:
Emails: a retry tells only what still stands, once, to whom it failed

- A decision's email (listing approved or refused, submitted, company
  verified or refused) checks the decision still stands, and a retry goes
  only to the member whose copy failed. Rebuilt for everybody after an edit
  bumped the listing's version, "your listing is live" went to every member
  again about a listing back in review.
- The status email follows the bell's rule for what is news: a candidate
  tidied back to a stage they were last told is not emailed again when that
  message's key has been pruned or was never claimed.
- The visibility notice keys on the day where the database has no
  visibility_chosen_at yet (before 336), instead of failing for good.
- An account suspended, restored and suspended again within the hour is
  emailed each time, keyed on the decision's audit record.
- The provider is sent the outbox row as its Idempotency-Key, so a message it
  accepted is not sent twice when only recording it failed; a 401 or 403
  (the key or the domain) waits like a missing key instead of dead-lettering
  every message on its first attempt.
- A listing's expiry notice is owed until every member who takes these emails
  has it; the weekly alert's next window starts where this one read the board.

scripts/email-retries.test.mjs: 25 checks, among them one per change that fails on the code before it;
notices.test.mjs holds the bell and the email to the same rule move by move.

Author: Claude
Message:
One-click unsubscribe that unsubscribes, and the profile reminder only for those who ask

The List-Unsubscribe header named the /unsubscribe page. RFC 8058 has a mail
client's own unsubscribe button POST `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` to that
address and take the answer as done; the page answers a POST by rendering
itself, so Gmail and Outlook got a 200 and nobody was unsubscribed. Every
preference email now carries both addresses (unsubscribeLinks): the footer
link opens the page, which asks first so a link scanner cannot unsubscribe
anybody, and the header names /api/unsubscribe, which makes the change.

The "finish your profile" reminder rode on notify_digest, a switch that is on
by default and labelled "weekly job roundup", and it is the one email here
that answers nothing the person asked for. It has its own switch now,
profiles.notify_profile_nudge, off unless turned on (migration 337), offered
on the website's and the app's email settings where the database has it; its
unsubscribe link turns off the reminder and nothing else. The recipient read
takes the whole profile row, so a database without the new switch cannot fail
every email's read, and the reminder stays off there.

email_log kept every recipient address forever ("decision required"). It is
delivery metadata, kept now for 180 days and pruned by the hourly maintenance
that already does it for notifications; a provider's failure reason is stored
with any address removed, as the warning beside it already was.

Tests: supabase/tests/email.test.mjs (the two addresses, the header and the
footer, the reminder's default, 180 days and what the prune leaves); app tests
for the switch where it exists and its absence where it does not. pnpm check
(website) and the app's pnpm check are green.

Report a listing or a company, and hide a company, from the app

The website's report dialog as a sheet, through its reportTarget action and
its rules: an account is required (a signed-out reader goes to sign in and

it back. The App Store asks for both in an app where people publish to one
another.

Author: Claude
Message:
Sign in on the phone: password, Apple, Google, email links, onboarding and the Account tab

The website's auth form, rule for rule, over Supabase Auth directly: eight
characters, GoTrue's refusals in the reader's language, a pause the server
can ask for, the confirmation email offered again, and Turnstile run from the
website's page in a hidden WebView when the project wants a captcha. Sign-up
asks for the website's own confirmation redirect, so the email works opened
anywhere; opened on the phone, /auth/confirm is verified in the app and lands
on onboarding with the door's role and the page the person was headed to.

Sign in with Apple natively (hashed nonce to Apple, the nonce to Supabase,
the name Apple gives once kept for onboarding) and Google through the system's
authentication browser with PKCE. An account with an authenticator is asked
for its code after any sign-in. Onboarding runs completeOnboarding and asks
for the Terms of use first. A session gate sends a session with no profile
there, however it arrived.

The Account tab: the doors when signed out; who is signed in, appearance,
the website, contact, signing out of this phone, and deleting the account —
for an Apple account after asking Apple for a fresh code so the grant is
revoked. /api/mobile/v1/config also carries SUPPORT_EMAIL.

Author: kirolosedward1
Message:
A failure somebody can quote: the support log, help requests and the account lookup

When something broke, the reader saw a generic sentence and the server wrote
one console line that Vercel keeps for an hour. Support could not answer a
single "it didn't work" without a developer reproducing it against production.
This is the database half of fixing that, and the helpers both sides share.

- BC-XXXX-XXXX references (src/lib/support/reference.ts): Crockford base32, so
  a reference retyped from a screenshot, in Arabic digits or with an O for a
  zero, still finds its row.
- Context that is safe to keep (src/lib/support/context.ts): a route is its
  path only, never the query or fragment where sign-in codes travel; a browser
  is described ("Chrome 128 · Android 14 · in-app Facebook"), not fingerprinted.
- Migration 200 adds the `support_replied` notification kind, alone, because
  Postgres will not use an enum value in the transaction that added it.
- Migration 201: support_events (one row per unexpected failure, keyed by the
  reference the reader saw, 90-day retention swept on write) and
  support_requests (the reader's words plus account, role, page, browser and
  build attached by the platform, idempotent per form). Writers are definer
  functions open to anon on purpose — sign-up and sign-in failures happen to
  signed-out people and production has no service-role key — and are capped
  per account, per address and across the signed-out side.
  admin_answer_support_request rings the bell once per distinct answer;
  admin_support_facts answers the usual ticket questions for one account
  without returning an address, a number, a file path or a CV.
- Numbered 200/201 because parallel branches already claim 68–110.

Nothing in the application calls any of this yet, so merging changes no
behaviour. The migrations are not applied to production.
